# TDP-006 — Failure Mode, Effects and Criticality Worksheet

**Author:** Nikhil Prakash (MASc, UBC ECE)
**Generated** by `docs/tdp/make_fmeca.py` from `docs/DEFECT_LOG.md`, `docs/thesis/cruxes.yaml` and `docs/THREAT_MODEL.md`. Do not edit by hand. Checked in CI; the severity-by-status counts are cross-checked against `docs/figures/dashboard_snapshot.json`.
**Format:** MIL-STD-1629A Task 101 worksheet columns, adapted to a software testbed: identification, item, function (plane), failure mode and cause, end effect (the thesis crux the defect bears on), detection method (the pass or review that found it), compensating provision (the fix or the recorded treatment), severity class. Format only. No failure rates or criticality numbers are computed: the testbed has no operating-hours data, and inventing a rate would violate guide rule 1.1.1.

## 1. Severity translation (declared once)

| Log letter | Log meaning | Worksheet class |
|---|---|---|
| H | affects a thesis claim or a security property | II Critical (affects a thesis claim or a security property) |
| M | wrong behaviour, bounded impact | III Marginal (wrong behaviour, bounded impact) |
| L | cosmetic or advisory | IV Minor (cosmetic or advisory) |

Class I (catastrophic) is not used: no failure of this testbed endangers life or equipment. The letter is the log's; the class is a translation of it, not a new rating.

## 4. Security goals and the adversary each counters (from the threat model)

| Goal | Statement | Countered adversary |
|---|---|---|
| G1 Authenticity | Only the controlling key can create/modify an identity or issue on its behalf | A1, A2 |
| G2 Non-forgeability of claims | A claim/attestation verifies only if signed by an authorized issuer over the bound context | A2 |
| G3 Replay resistance | A captured signed operation/presentation cannot be re-used out of context (nonce/domain/chain binding). *Narrowed 2026-10-10 (WM-1 audit U-F8, defect D52):* ERC-1056's signed operations bind the registry address and a nonce but **not the chain id**, so a signa … | A1 |
| G4 Authorization integrity | A party cannot act beyond its role (issue/attest/revoke) | A2 |
| G5 Sybil cost | Creating N identities imposes a cost/gate proportional to N | A2 |
| G6 Recoverability | A compromised key need not mean permanent identity loss | A3 |
| G7 PII confidentiality | The VIN and linkable PII do not appear in plaintext on-chain | A4 |
| G8 Theft resistance | Transferring/stealing a token or key does not silently transfer the whole identity where the design forbids it | A2, A3 |

## 5. Reading rule

A row with severity H and status other than fixed blocks every chapter claim on its path (`docs/DEFECT_LOG.md` section D). A row with status fixed names its commit in the compensating-provision column; the regression test that holds it is in the layer that owns the path (guide rule 1.2.5).
